title: Project Mclaren - Capital A x Basis

sentences.text: So I oversee corporate development and business development Basis, you alluded to it earlier.
We're fairly established company.
We were founded back in 2001, so we like to think of ourselves as the oldest independent ad tech company.
Whether that's true or not, I've never spent the time to try and figure it out.
But we've been around for a long time.

Company originally started doing more managed service for agencies, working with holding companies that we're trying to navigate digital activation, but specifically through regional or local efforts.
As the company expanded through the years and our customer base grew, we moved more to just full digital activation.
No longer focused on the local regional aspect, but that's still a component of our business.
But we're doing as much national and international as local and regional at this point.
900 employees headquartered in Chicago.
We go to market with kind of a hybrid model.
So we lead with basis platform, which is our technology.
So you guys have a great time.
And so that will be licensed out to agencies or brands that are doing in house for digital activation, typically in a hybrid model.
So we license the platform on a seat license basis.
But then we also have our proprietary DSP that's built within the core of basis platform itself.
And that goes as typical DSP pricing models, percent of media, type of approach, and we'll negotiate based off of what our customer spend thresholds are and where they're trying to go from there.
Basis platform holistically supports search, social, programmatic, direct buying from an activation standpoint, but also reporting and analytics.
And then you know, obviously across the board there we do any kind of digital activation.
So whether it's ctv, streaming audio, digital out of home, classic display, you know, et cetera, if it's got a digital screen, you can activate and measure it through basis platform.
What is interesting and what kind of raised my interest on TSG was twofold.
So the vast majority of our business is domestic in the US so I'd say 85% is North America and then probably call it 7 to 8% Latam and then the rest predominantly EU.
But there's never really been a big focus or a big push by us to enter the European Unit Union.
So, you know, one of the strategies we've been thinking about is, you know, is this a pathway for us to use activation or use an acquisition as a means to help build that footprint.

So looking and seeing if we can find complementary technology and solutioning that, you know, one we can bring to the states if it doesn't have scale, but then two, to help us use as kind of a launching pad for, you know, what we hope to.
What we hope to do within the union itself.
Retail media for us has been an area where we do light and loose activation.
I'd say.
I'd say there's not really a strong push by us at this moment.
What we're doing predominantly is PMP enabled.
Right.
So we're taking retail media networks, taking data, turning that into private marketplace deals that our customers can leverage within the platform itself.
And then that is predominantly what the offering is today.
There isn't any kind of additional measurement solutions.
We're not talking about incremental roas, any of those capabilities.
So that would be the other aspect to me, which becomes kind of interesting is not having that retail solution and not having a strong EU presence.
To me feels like there might be some synergies that I wanted to explore further with with gsg.
Brilliant.
Yeah.
I mean, what a great fit.
And also their platform is called Base as well.
So I did see that could fit.
Right in there with what you're doing already without a brand change, which is great.

So, yeah, they are really strong in the uk, they've got one of the big supermarkets here as a client and as well as some of the big French hypermarkets as well in Europe and they are also in Australia.
So they've got quite a mix of business and are growing very quickly on their SaaS offering as well.
So it could be a really good fit.
Obviously there's a huge market in the us which I guess in some ways is untapped, particularly the sort of middle tier because there's so many of the biggest are already.
I mean, they're up and running already and Amazon's one of them.
So it's already pretty big, but there's a sort of middle tier and they don't have huge access to this kind of stuff.
So there is a big opportunity for an American buyer to be able to bring this to the States as well for that tier.
So, yeah, very exciting opportunity.
Whereabouts are you?
I heard you say goodbye to your kids.
I hope that wasn't the final goodbye.
But are you.
Hey, they're like the cat that won't die, man.
They always come back.
So don't worry, we say goodbye, but we'll see them later today.
Kind of non committal.
See you later.
Yeah, you're around this week to get something set up straight away because it's a deal that we're looking to get closed in the next month or get offers on the table in the next month or Two as well.
So if you guys are around this week and we can get call set up and then we can get things going.
If you're interested in moving forward, what's your kind of window for acquisitions?
Have you done a ton previously and you're looking to close or is it quite sort of slow approach?
I mean, I'll be honest with you, we've done, I've been with the company 16 years.
During that time, we've done three acquisitions.
It amazes me how long they end up taking typically on our side.
Here's what I'd say with, with Cannes lion coming up next week, we've got people that are all over the place, either in preparation for that or else getting ready for it here at Stateside.
So trying to get a good meeting.
That was part of the reason why I checked with Ahmad to see whether or not there might be an opportunity for a face to face in can next week.

I think we're looking for the end of July.
So there's, there's plenty of space.
Not like a mad rush to get it done, but get something before the start of August because August is a ball.

summary.overview: The Exploratory Business Development Call focused on the potential partnership between Basis, an established independent ad tech company, and TSG, a rapidly growing SaaS provider. Basis provided an overview of its evolution from managed services to comprehensive digital activation across various channels, highlighting its current market presence—with 85% of its business in North America and a goal to enhance its footprint in the European Union through strategic acquisition. Both parties identified synergies, particularly with TSG's established retail media capabilities in the UK and beyond. The meeting included discussions on the structure of TSG's services, encompassing consulting and proprietary technology solutions, and set action items for follow-up, including scheduling a platform demonstration and a potential face-to-face meeting at the Cannes Lions festival.
summary.short_summary: The Exploratory Business Development Call centered on the partnership potential between Basis, an independent ad tech company, and TSG, a rapidly growing SaaS provider. Basis, founded in 2001 and headquartered in Chicago, has evolved from managed services to comprehensive digital activation, with 85% of its business in North America and a goal to expand into the European Union through acquisitions. The discussion highlighted TSG's established retail media capabilities in the UK and its growth in SaaS offerings, identifying synergies between the two companies. Action items included scheduling a platform demonstration and a potential face-to-face meeting at the Cannes Lions festival. Both parties recognized the need for a more robust retail solution in the EU and explored the structure of TSG's consulting and proprietary technology services.
